notes: EMBERWAKE — an original 3D momentum-glider game built on a custom WebGL2 engine (no external libraries, assets or network use; runs from index.html on static hosting and from file://). The sun has set on a sealed 2.4 km valley; you pilot a lantern-glider that trades altitude for speed (energy-conserving arcade aerodynamics with stall, banked turns and boost), ride thermals, graze stone for fuel, dodge drifting storm cells and light eight sleeping beacons — each a checkpoint that warms the world — then fly the Dawn Gate on the summit for a dusk-to-dawn finale with stats. 3D is the mechanic: dive-for-speed/climb-to-spend energy trading, landmark line-of-sight navigation via beacon light pillars and a compass, altitude gates (a floating isle reachable by thermal or boost), terrain/prop/water collision with soft-fail scraping and hard-crash respawn. All content is procedural or hand-authored in code: 83k-vertex heightmapped terrain with baked AO vertex color, 2800 instanced swaying trees, spires/arches/buttes/floating isles, analytic sky with sun/stars/clouds, shader water, instanced billboard particles, and a fully synthesised WebAudio layer (speed-mapped wind, drone pad that rises with progress, pentatonic pickups, thunder, dawn chords). Accessibility: keyboard-path menus with focus states, aria-live compass callouts, labelled settings (quality/sensitivity/invert/volume/reduced-motion/touch), reduced-motion support, never colour-only meaning. Verified with automated headless-Chrome (CDP) runs: full loop (title, flight, dive/boost, steering, ember pickup, beacon ignition, crash/respawn, pause, all-beacon gate pass, finale, completion panel, keep-soaring, 700px viewport) with zero console errors and zero exceptions, plus a headless CPU simulation of the flight model; file:// boot also verified clean. Known limitations: FPS was measured in headless Chrome (20-30 fps under screencast, software-limited) so real-GPU smoothness is unverified on physical hardware here; touch controls were exercised via their DOM logic but not with a real touchscreen; WebGL2 is required (a styled error screen shows otherwise); no shadow maps (baked AO + hemisphere lighting instead).
